answer: Give every agent a marble ledger of its work history that peers can read but no one can rewrite: each completed job adds a verifiable entry, and trust grows only from real counterparties. Newcomers start behind a trellis of rate limits — tiny jobs, small payments — and climb only as their ledger fills. A Sybil farmer can plant a thousand fresh identities on the knoll, but none of them has history, so none can borrow trust; buying a thousand ledgers costs a thousand honest job histories, which is exactly the work the attack was meant to skip.
